notes: §1985:XVI.3.3.4 SR2: a SORT in a non-independent segment may name a procedure "Wholly contained in a single independent segment". Segmentation.RangeAllowed, asked per procedure from SortBinder.SortBindFile/CheckSegmentation at 85, admits one independent segment and refuses two (COBOL6877); the witness INPUT PROCEDURE 60 THRU 70 from segment 0 is refused. Probes at --std 85 (work-rd-11): each procedure is checked on its own at its phrase (SortBinder.CheckSegmentation): s01 SORT in segment 0 with INPUT in 60 and OUTPUT in 70 accepted and ran (A B DONE), s02 SORT in 60 with INPUT in 60 and OUTPUT in fixed 20 ran (A B DONE), s03 SORT in 60 USING F1 OUTPUT in 70 refused COBOL6877, s07 SORT USING/GIVING (sequential files, no procedures) in 60 ran (A); c edition arm: a segment-number at 2002/2014/2023 is COBOL0902 and --permissive does not ask the rule (e01); a, d, f do not reach a procedure-placement rule. The procedures are the NAMED ones (docs/CONFORMANCE.md 3.8).

next.reason: 1985: "If a SORT statement appears in an independent segment, then any input procedures or output procedures ... must be contained"; 2023: "No 2023 clause holds the Segmentation feature; no candidate deals with independent segments". Independent segments (Segmentation module) have no 2023 counterpart. The SORT/MERGE candidates restrict SORT statements and procedures but say nothing about segment placement.
